## Failing test suites <!--26142098515-->
Commit: 7db3f22be7ad679ed3fad0d9e33ef0d7789dc529

`__NEXT_EXPERIMENTAL_PPR=true pnpm test-dev test/development/app-hmr/hmr.test.ts` (PPR)
- app-dir-hmr > filesystem changes > should update server components after navigating to a page with a different runtime

<details>
<summary>Expand output</summary>

  ● app-dir-hmr › filesystem changes › should update server components after navigating to a page with a different runtime

    expect(received).toEqual(expected) // deep equality

    - Expected  - 1
    + Received  + 1

      Object {
    -   "envValue": "mac",
    +   "envValue": "ipad",
        "mpa": false,
      }

      118 |         // B. triggers error on server resulting in MPA: `{ envValue: 'ipad', mpa: true }` and server logs: ⨯ [TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'polyfillFiles')] ⨯ [TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'default')]
      119 |         // A is more common than B.
    > 120 |         expect({ envValue, mpa }).toEqual({
          |                                   ^
      121 |           envValue:
      122 |             isPPREnabledByDefault && !process.env.TURBOPACK
      123 |               ? // FIXME: Should be 'ipad' but PPR+Webpack swallows the update reliably

      at Object.toEqual (development/app-hmr/hmr.test.ts:120:35)

</details>


Read more about building and testing Next.js in [contributing.md](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/contributing.md).

body:
I think a warning would be better in this case, for example: generating pages from a CMS.

People might not notice the generated params was empty and the error "no generateStaticParams" is misleading.
author: fuma-nama

body:
> People might not notice the generated params was empty and the error "no generateStaticParams" is misleading.

Isn't that an argument for failing instead of warning? From my experience, warnings are most often missed.

I agree that the current message is misleading but that doesn't imply we should downgrade to a warning. We could adjust the error message if the function returns an empty result instead.

body: I see your point, I will change the error message instead

body: Hi @leerob, thanks for the feedback, so maybe the ideal would be to keep the current documentation and add a part in the documentation that explains how to use it and specifies that it's experimental?
author: antoinekm

body: And also, do we keep it in the templates or add it when it's really been tested and approved?
author: antoinekm

body:
I've removed all the changes I've made to the documentation, because with hindsight, it will be preferable to integrate it gradually, depending on whether or not the community adopts this feature.
So I've only added to the documentation how it's used, I've also specified that it's experimental.
author: antoinekm

body: Even tho it's used in all the popular frameworks but what's the usecase of it when u can import the type and use it? Using a fn adds some runtime processing too and using ts type, you are still getting all the autocompletes
author: imranbarbhuiya

body:
> Even tho it's used in all the popular frameworks but what's the usecase of it when u can import the type and use it? Using a fn adds some runtime processing too and using ts type, you are still getting all the autocompletes

Hey @imranbarbhuiya, I would say:
- Consistency across the ecosystem: Adopting this model in Next.js helps maintain consistency between frameworks.
- Code cleanliness: There's no need to explicitly annotate types everywhere (especially since new developers will probably have trouble understanding what they are), reducing boilerplate and making the configuration file easier to read/maintain.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Keep in mind that this isn't the game changer, it should be seen as a help for newcomers and/or a way of aligning with competing frameworks and their users migrating to/learning Next.js.
author: antoinekm

body: Thank you for this suggestion. I have more conviction now that I don't believe it's the right time to add a feature like this with Next.js 15 adding `next.config.ts` support. Side note: in the future, I would recommend making a Discussion with a proposal for the feature before making a PR, such that it can get upvotes and community feedback.
